summary:
Bullpen is the category to build around today, hot across all three ratings (+7.0pts each) and running 109-79 (58%) over the last 14 days for R1, R2, and R3 alike. Hitting is worth a look too, but only for R1 — it's flashing +7.4pts and 108-80 (57%) there, while it sits flat at 48% for R2 and R3, so treat that edge as rating-specific. The bigger warning sign is sp, which is cold across the board (-6.3 to -7.9pts, 42-45% over the last 14 days) — fade any pick leaning on starting pitcher logic right now. Also note bullpen_fatigue is stuck in an 8-game losing streak at 48% across every rating; it's dead weight until it breaks. On category combos, trends+runs remains the model's best agreement pair at 56.5% (208-160, n=368), with trends+bullpen right behind at 55.7% — stacking either with today's bullpen heat is the strongest setup available.

On rating strength, R3 is the unit leader with season +35.0u and a hot 14-day stretch at 51% (+8.0u, n=81), plus a strong 30-day run at +18.0u. R1 isn't far behind with +27.0u season and the best 7-day number (+5.0u, 48%), while R2 is the laggard, bleeding -1.0u over the last 30 days despite matching R1/R3 on season totals. If you're choosing between ratings today, lean R3 or R1 over R2.

Team-wise, TBR is the clear go-to when the model likes them — 23-8 (74%) overall and an elite 18-4 (82%, +23.0u) on strong plays, the best combination of volume and profit on the board. BOS (76%, n=33) and CHC (75%, n=24) are also chalk-worthy. Avoid leaning on HOU strong plays — 2-7 (22%, -8.0u) is a clear red flag despite a respectable 60% base rate, and BAL's strong record (4-7, -3.0u) says the same. Best stack today: R1 or R3, bullpen-driven, trends+runs agreement, with TBR or BOS involved if they show up on the board.
